1. A 46-year-old woman presents to her primary care doctor to request a referral to ophthalmology.
2. Her vision has been steadily declining over the past 2 years and she thinks she needs a prescription for glasses.
3. She further complains that her lips and feet feel numb.
4. Her medical history is notable for medullary thyroid cancer status post total thyroidectomy.
5. Her periods are regular.
6. She enjoys a diverse diet and takes levothyroxine.
7. Her blood pressure is 110/70 mmHg, pulse is 80/min, and respirations are 12/min.
8. She is alert and oriented.
9. Her pupils are equal, round, and reactive to light, but appear opacified.
10. Extraocular movements are intact, albeit slow.
11. Her visual acuity is decreased bilaterally.
12. The remainder of her physical exam is unremarkable.
13. Her basic metabolic panel is shown below: Na+: 139 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L K+: 4.9 mEq/L HCO3-: 25 mEq/L BUN: 10 mg/dL Glucose: 110 mg/dL Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dL Thyroid-stimulating hormone: 1.5 µU/mL Ca2+: 7.0 mEq/L Phosphorus: 6.5 mEq/L Albumin: 3.6 mg/dL The patient's ECG is shown in Figure A.

1. A 46-year-old male with a past medical history of hypertension presents to the clinic with lower back pain.  
2. He reports the pain began 3 months ago and has progressively worsened, which is interfering with his job as a truck driver.  
3. He describes the pain as achy, and it is exacerbated by driving for prolonged periods of time without rest.  
4. He denies taking any medications.  
5. The patient’s vital signs reveal:  

| Temperature | 37°C (98.8°F) |  
| --- | --- |  
| Blood pressure | 152/90 mm Hg |  
| Heart rate | 86/min |  
| Body mass index | 40 kg/m2 |  

On physical examination, there is exquisite tenderness to palpation in the paravertebral musculature of the lower lumbar and sacral regions.  
6. The right transverse process of L5 is notably posterior and does not change in flexion or extension.  
7. The right inferior lateral angle is superior to the left, and a spring test is negative.

1. A 22-year-old woman comes to the physician in October for a follow-up examination.
2. She feels well.
3. She has a 2-year history of type 1 diabetes mellitus controlled with insulin.
4. She had a normal Pap smear 3 months ago and saw her ophthalmologist 6 months ago.
5. Her 67-year-old grandmother has breast cancer.
6. She is 168 cm (5 ft 6 in) tall and weighs 57 kg (125 lb); BMI is 20 kg/m2 .
7. Her hemoglobin A1c is 6.2%, and fingerstick blood glucose concentration is 118 mg/dL.

1. A 1-year-old girl is brought to a neurologist due to increasing seizure frequency over the past 2 months.
2. She recently underwent a neurology evaluation which revealed hypsarrhythmia on electroencephalography (EEG) with a mix of slow waves, multifocal spikes, and asynchrony.
3. Her parents have noticed the patient occasionally stiffens and spreads her arms at home.
4. She was born at 38-weeks gestational age without complications.
5. She has no other medical problems.
6. Her medications consist of lamotrigine and valproic acid.
7. Her temperature is 98.3°F (36.8°C), blood pressure is 90/75 mmHg, pulse is 94/min, and respirations are 22/min.
8. Physical exam reveals innumerable hypopigmented macules on the skin and an irregularly shaped, thickened, and elevated plaque on the lower back.

1. A 34-year-old primigravid woman at 20 weeks' gestation presents for follow-up after discovering a mass in her left breast two weeks ago.
2. She experienced menarche at age 11, and her menstrual cycles occurred every 30–40 days prior to pregnancy.
3. Her vital signs are normal.
4. Physical examination reveals a 3-cm, firm, nonmobile, nontender mass in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast, with no palpable axillary lymphadenopathy.
5. Pelvic examination confirms a uterus size consistent with 20 weeks of gestation.
6. Ultrasound and core biopsy confirm infiltrating lobular carcinoma, with the pathological specimen testing positive for estrogen and ERBB2 receptors and negative for progesterone receptors.
7. Staging reveals no evidence of distant metastases.

1. A 49-year-old man presents with 3 months of generalized weakness.
2. He has had a chronic cough and a 20 pound unintentional weight loss over the past 6 months.
3. He has a medical history significant for high blood pressure, hyperlipidemia, and seasonal allergies with no prior surgical history.
4. He has no history of tobacco use.
5. He moved from India 7 years prior to presentation.
6. He currently lives in Oregon and has not left the west coast since moving.
7. His temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 100/70 mmHg, pulse is 76/min, and respirations are 16/min.
8. His physical exam is significant for hyperpigmentation of the oral mucosa and temporal muscle wasting.
9. Radiography of the abdomen demonstrates bilateral adrenal calcifications.

1. A 37-year-old male with no significant medical history presents with an 8-week history of burning epigastric pain that occurs post-prandially and occasionally radiates to his back.
2. He reports early satiety and postprandial bloating but denies weight loss or changes in bowel habits.
3. His social history includes moderate alcohol consumption (1-3 beers weekly) and no smoking.
4. Physical examination reveals mild epigastric tenderness without guarding or rebound tenderness, normal bowel sounds, and is otherwise unremarkable.

1. A woman in her 70s presented with a 3-month history of episodic fever and painless cutaneous lesions on her lower limbs.
2. The patient otherwise felt well and denied malaise, weight loss, or any other symptoms.
3. She did not have any known benign inflammatory conditions.
4. Physical examination showed indurated plaques with multiple telangiectasias (Figure, A and B) on almost all the surface of the legs.
5. Except for slightly elevated C-reactive protein levels, the results of other routine blood and urine tests were unremarkable.
6. A skin biopsy specimen was obtained for histopathology examination (Figure, C and D).
7. A, Indurated violaceous plaques with multiple telangiectasias on the lower limbs.
8. B, Prominent telangiectasia on the thigh.
9. C, Histopathologic analysis shows large round cells proliferating within dermal blood vessels (hematoxylin-eosin).
10. D, Round cells with scanty cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli filling a vessel (hematoxylin-eosin).

1. A 15-year-old male presents to the office with the complaint of painless swelling in the left testicle that has varied in size over the past several months.  
2. There is no history of trauma.  
3. The lesion transilluminates well, and no inguinal nodes are palpable.  
4. Findings from a testicular scan are normal.

1. A 55-year-old man presents to the emergency department with chest pressure and diaphoresis.
2. His symptoms started at work when he was lifting boxes.
3. He states that he currently feels crushing pressure over his chest.
4. He is given aspirin and an ECG is performed in triage, as seen in Figure A.
5. His past medical history is notable for diabetes and obesity.
6. He has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes per day for the past 30 years.
7. His temperature is 97.9°F (36.6°C), blood pressure is 155/99 mmHg, pulse is 110/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air.
8. Physical exam reveals an uncomfortable, diaphoretic man.
9. His heart and breath sounds are unremarkable.
10. A repeat ECG in the emergency department is performed, also seen in Figure A.
11. The patient’s chest pain is worse when the ECG in the emergency department is taken, compared to the one taken in triage.
12. He is given nitroglycerin, with minimal improvement in his symptoms.
13. A troponin level is drawn.

1. A 27-year-old woman presents to the emergency department for bilateral, painful loss of vision.
2. Her symptoms started last night and have persisted until this morning.
3. She has experienced an episode of urinary incontinence as well.
4. The patient has a medical history of anxiety as well as peripheral neuropathy which is currently treated with duloxetine.
5. Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 100/60 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air.
6. On physical exam, the patient demonstrates 4/5 strength in her upper and lower extremities with decreased sensation in her fingers bilaterally.
7. An MRI is obtained and is within normal limits.

1. Patient D is a 65-year-old  female with 5 months of mid back pain
2. Patient D states that the pain has gradually reached peak intensity and now interrupts her sleep
3. No medications have helped with her pain
4. When you perform a physical exam, you find that she has diminished sensation in her mid thoracic dermatomes, and her back is not tender to palpation
5. You also note that her eyes and mucous membranes were more pale than normal
6. Concerned for this constellation of signs/symptoms, you order for MRI of her thoracic spine, which reveals a large mass involving the gastric body and extending posteriorly into the spinal column
7. You also note multiple additional lesions in several distant regions of the thorax
8.

1. A 23-year-old woman is admitted to the inpatient psychiatry unit after her boyfriend reported she was “acting funny and refusing to talk.” The patient’s boyfriend states that he came home from work and found the patient sitting up in bed staring at the wall.
2. When he said her name or waved his hand in front of her, she did not respond.
3. When he tried to move her, she would remain in whatever position she was placed.
4. Her temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 122/79 mmHg, pulse is 68/min, and respirations are 12/min with an oxygen saturation of 98% on room air.
5. The patient is lying on the bed with her left arm raised and pointing at the ceiling.
6. She resists any attempt to change her position.
7. The patient remains mute and ignores any external stimuli.
8. The patient’s medical history is significant for depression.
9. She was recently switched from phenelzine to fluoxetine.

1. A 51-year-old female with multiple comorbidities including HIV/AIDS, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and a history of infectious mononucleosis presents with fatigue and weakness.
2. She has a daily consumption of one pack of cigarettes and one glass of wine.
3. Her vital signs are stable, but examination reveals bounding pulses, pallor, and an enlarged cervical lymph node.
4. After being diagnosed with diffuse bulky Burkitt lymphoma and starting chemotherapy, she develops decreased urinary output eight days into treatment.

1. A new blood test to detect prostate cancer is evaluated in 300 male volunteers.
2. A needle biopsy of the prostate gland is done on all men with serum prostate-specific antigen concentrations greater than 5 ng/mL (N<4).
3. One hundred men undergo biopsy procedures; 90 are found to have prostate cancer, and five are found to have chronic prostatitis.

1. A 40-year-old man arrives at the emergency department presenting with gastrointestinal symptoms including abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and profuse watery diarrhea.
2. He also reports experiencing a metallic taste and a dry, persistent cough.
3. The patient recently returned from camping where he consumed well water exclusively.
4. He takes multiple homeopathic supplements but no prescription medications.
5. His vital signs show: temperature 98.7°F, blood pressure 100/60 mmHg, heart rate 100/min, and respiratory rate 16/min.
6. Clinical examination reveals a garlic-like breath odor and skin pigmentation changes.
7. The ECG shows QT interval prolongation across all leads.
8. This poisoning is known to interfere with the connection between glycolysis and the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle.

1. Patient D is a 44-year-old  female who presents with 2 months of low-back and leg pain
2. The pain started after a day of heavy yard work and has progressed gradually over time
3. Patient D describes the pain as a dull ache in her lower back that is accompanied by intense shooting pains down her leg to the sole of her left foot
4. In the last three weeks, she endorses tripping and stumbling more frequently, and has been told by friends that she is dragging her left foot
5. At present time she is most concerned about the increasing severity of pain, which is affecting her ability to function
6. When you examine Patient D, you confirm that she has a left foot drop with diminished sensation in the sole of her foot
7. You order an MRI, which reveals an L5-S1 disc herniation with associated canal stenosis and left neuroforaminal stenosis
8.

1. A 30-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of intermittent fevers, chills, malaise, and fatigue for the past month.
2. The symptoms develop sporadically, last anywhere from 1-4 days, and spontaneously resolve.
3. The patient returned from a safari trip in Africa 2-months ago.
4. He received chemoprophylaxis with chloroquine during the trip and continued it for four weeks after returning.
5. Past medical history is unremarkable.
6. Temperature is 38.9°C (102.0°F), pulse is 103/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 118/70 mmHg.
7. Physical examination shows pale conjunctiva and an enlarged spleen.
8. Peripheral blood smear shows trophozoites and schizonts.

1. A 45-year-old man comes to the physician because of right shoulder pain that began after he chopped wood 2 days ago.  
2. Examination of the right upper extremity shows no obvious bone deformities or point tenderness.  
3. The pain is reproduced when the patient is asked to externally rotate the shoulder against resistance; there is no weakness.

1. A 44-year-old female presents to the office for evaluation of a lump on her neck that she noted 1 week ago.
2. She denies any tenderness, fever, weight loss, or fatigue.
3. Physical examination reveals a 2-cm freely movable mass in the lower left lobe of the thyroid.

1. Patient D is a 44-year-old  female presenting with severe left flank pain
2. Patient D's pain occurs intermittently every and lasts approximately 30 minutes at a time
3. Patient D describes the pain as sometimes radiating to her groin area
4. Patient D endorses generally poor water intake, and a family history of kidney stones
5. Patient D's urinalysis is positive for blood, and a CT scan of her abdomen reveals multiple stones at the left ureteropelvic junction
6. Just as she is leaving the scanner, she begins to experience another episode of flank pain, and screams in agony.

1. A woman in her 60s with a history of hyperlipidemia, hypothyroidism, and chronic migraines presented with 9 months of progressively worsening left-sided ptosis, which was more notable at night and with fatigue.
2. She denied experiencing pain, diplopia, muscle weakness, dysarthria, dysphagia, difficulty breathing, or other neurologic deficits.
3. On examination, corrected visual acuity was 20/20 bilaterally, with normal color vision, visual fields, intraocular pressure, extraocular movements, alignment, and pupils.
4. External examination was notable for left upper eyelid ptosis (Figure 1), with a margin-to-reflex distance 1 of 3.5 mm on the right and 0.5 mm on the left, intact levator function, and no fatiguability on sustained upgaze.
5. There was no evidence of eyelid edema, erythema, or tenderness to palpation.
6. There were no palpable adnexal masses or orbital rim deformities, but there was mild fullness in the left superior sulcus and mildly increased left-sided resistance to retropulsion.
7. However, Hertel exophthalmometry did not reveal any relative proptosis.
8. No lacrimal gland abnormalities or conjunctival masses were seen with upper eyelid eversion.
9. There was no palpable preauricular or cervical lymphadenopathy.
10. Slitlamp and fundus examination findings were normal.
11. Serological testing results for antiacetylcholine receptor antibody were negative.

1. A 72-year-old man presents to the office with a 5-month history of persistent lower back pain.
2. He describes the pain as dull and as worsening with prolonged standing or when lifting heavy objects.
3. The patient denies any trauma.
4. He requests osteopathic manipulative treatment with high-velocity low-amplitude (HVLA) because the technique helped him with pain relief in the past.
5. Past medical history is significant for prostate cancer that was diagnosed 3 years ago and treated with radiation therapy.
6. Further review of records reveals multiple metastatic lesions to the spine.

1. A 57-year-old woman with a medical history of recurrent biliary colic was admitted with symptoms consistent with mild gallstone pancreatitis.
2. Routine laboratory test results showed total bilirubin of 4.74 mg/dL (to convert to millimoles per liter, multiply by 17.104) and amylase of 1.041 U/L (to convert to microkatals per liter, multiply by 0.0167).
3. An abdominal ultrasonography scan demonstrated gallstones and a mildly dilated common bile duct (CBD).
4. Magnetic resonance imaging of the abdomen confirmed these results and revealed cholelithiasis.
5. The patient consequently underwent urgent laparoscopic cholecystectomy with intraoperative cholangiography (Figure, A).
6. Intraoperative cholangiography revealed an unusual anatomical variant and subsequent transcystic choledochoscopy was performed, which demonstrated a double lumen at the distal CBD (Figure, B).
7. Multiple gallstones were found within a dilated region of cystic duct.

1. A young girl presented to establish care for skin lesions on her trunk and extremities that had been present since birth.
2. Her mother described an intermittent inflammatory reaction localized only to the patient’s abnormal skin lesions that was reproducible in febrile states and was concerned about asymptomatic, stable, dark brown lesions that had developed in areas of prior blistering and scarring on the patient’s right arm, left knee, and right upper back.
3. There was no history of developmental delay, eye abnormalities, or seizures.
4. Examination revealed irregular, dark brown, well-demarcated macules with regular pigment networks on dermoscopy within prominent soft, yellow, papular protrusions in a Blaschkolinear arrangement on her upper arms, particularly her right arm.
5. The right flank demonstrated linear, atrophic pink plaques with focal erosions and crusting, evidencing recent inflammation described by the patient’s mother (Figure, A).
6. Additional irregular, well-demarcated, evenly pigmented dark brown macules were present within pink, atrophic scars located on the right side of the trunk, the right upper back, and the left knee.
7. She had well-healed surgical scars on the hands, syndactyly of the toes, and ventral pterygium and dystrophy of the fingernails and toenails (Figure, B).
8. A, Irregular, dark brown, well-demarcated macules within prominent soft, yellow, papular protrusions in a Blaschkolinear arrangement on the upper arms; linear, atrophic pink plaques with focal erosions and crusting are seen on the right flank.
9. B, Extracutaneous features show syndactyly of the toes and ventral pterygium and dystrophy of the toe nails.
10. C, Hematoxylin-eosin staining of skin biopsy demonstrates close proximity of subcutaneous fat to the epidermis with attenuated collagen (original magnification × 20).
11. Previous treatment had included surgical excision of a frequently symptomatic focus of affected skin with subsequent adjacent tissue transfer.
12. Additionally, she had received dental implantation of frontal upper incisors.
13. Histopathologic slides from the prior excision of affected skin were reviewed (Figure, C).

1. A 41-year-old woman presented with a rapidly growing, painful nodule on her upper cutaneous lip (Figure, A) as well as several smaller papules on her face and neck, all of which had developed within the preceding 6 months.
2. She was otherwise asymptomatic.A, Centrally depressed, firm, pink 1.1-cm nodule on the upper cutaneous lip and skin-colored papule on the left medial cheek (above marker dots).
3. B, Cup-shaped tumor demonstrated keratinocyte atypia with a central core of keratinaceous debris.
4. C, Sebaceous tumor with a modestly increased ratio of basaloid cells to sebocytes.The patient’s medical history included diabetes mellitus type 2, hypercholesterolemia, hypertension, and depression.
5. Review of her family medical history revealed that her paternal grandfather died from melanoma and that her father died from colon cancer.
6. She stated that most of the men in her family had died from some form of cancer by the fourth decade of life.On physical examination, a tender, centrally depressed, firm, pink 1.1-cm nodule was present on her upper cutaneous lip (Figure, A).
7. Three other skin-colored to pink papules were present on her face and neck.
8. Shave biopsies of all 4 skin lesions were performed (Figure, B and C).

1. A 55-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by his wife because of a 1-hour history of nausea, dizziness, and confusion.  
2. Five hours ago, he told his wife he ingested a handful of pills “to put an end to it all.” He has hypertension, atrial fibrillation, low back pain, and major depressive disorder.  
3. His medications are ramipril, metoprolol, acetaminophen, and nortriptyline.  
4. On arrival, he is awake but confused.  
5. His temperature is 39.0°C (102.2°F), pulse is 120/min, respirations are 10/min, and blood pressure is 100/75 mm Hg.  
6. Examination shows dilated pupils and dry, flushed skin.  
7. The abdomen is distended, and there is diffuse tenderness to palpation; there is no guarding or rebound.  
8. Bowel sounds are hypoactive.

1. A 37-year-old Anglo-American man is admitted to the hospital for treatment for cocaine dependency.  
2. He says he has tried repeatedly to abstain from cocaine use but lives in a part of town where there are heavy drug sales.  
3. He did not like his hospital outpatient group but liked his single session at Cocaine Anonymous.  
4. Vital signs are temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse 70/min, respirations 16/min, and blood pressure 125/85 mm Hg.  
5. Physical examination shows a thin man with good muscle strength and no focal neurologic deficits.  
6. The patient is using insurance coverage through his wife but does not wish for his diagnosis to be disclosed to anyone.  
7. He is on probation after a conviction for aggravated robbery 3 years ago.  
8. There is also a warrant for his arrest for assault and battery.

1. A 67-year-old woman comes to the physician because of easy bruising for 4 months.
2. She has a history of lung cancer treated with radiation therapy 6 months ago.
3. She has a 2-year history of hypertension treated with a thiazide diuretic and an angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor.
4. Examination, including neurologic examination, shows no abnormalities except for multiple ecchymoses.
5. Her hemoglobin concentration is 13 g/dL, leukocyte count is 5000/mm3 , and platelet count is 35,000/mm3 .
6. A serum antiplatelet antibody assay is negative.

1. A 5-year-old girl presents to the emergency room due to difficulty walking.
2. She has been complaining of pain in her right leg for the last few days.
3. Her neighbor’s cat bit her last week and her parents attributed the pain to her healing bite.
4. At the time of the bite, they cleaned the wound and irrigated it with sterile saline water from a first aid kit.
5. She has no medical history and has never been hospitalized.
6. Her temperature is 102.2°F (39°C), blood pressure is 118/78 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 21/min, and pulse oximetry is 99% on room air.
7. The open wound remains present on the thigh with surrounding erythema and edema.
8. MRI is consistent with osteomyelitis.

1. A 62-year-old man presents to the emergency department with chest pain and shortness of breath that he experienced while barbecuing.
2. The pain is over his chest and in his left arm.
3. The patient has a medical history of obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.
4. His current medications include insulin, metformin, lisinopril, and hydrochlorothiazide.
5. An ECG is performed and is seen in Figure A.
6. His temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), pulse is 112/min, blood pressure is 100/70 mmHg, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air.
7. The patient is appropriately managed and is admitted to the step-down unit.
8. 2 days later, he complains of chest pain.
9. A repeat ECG is performed and is seen in Figure B.

1. A 13-month-old boy is in the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) with bronchiolitis and impending respiratory failure.  
2. He was born at 30 weeks’ gestation and required continuous positive airway pressure in the neonatal intensive care unit for one week before being discharged home without any requirements for supplemental oxygen.  
3. During his current hospitalization, he has undergone several trials of noninvasive support, but he continues to have markedly increased work of breathing, with blood gas testing confirming hypercapnia.  
4. A decision is made to intubate the patient and place him on mechanical ventilation.

1. Twelve hours after birth, a 2700-g (5-lb 15-oz) male newborn presents with three episodes of bilious vomiting.
2. He was delivered at 36 weeks' gestation to a 27-year-old mother whose pregnancy was complicated by polyhydramnios.
3. The mother has a history of smoking half a pack of cigarettes daily and intravenous cocaine use.
4. The newborn's vital signs are stable.
5. On examination, his upper abdomen is distended, and bowel sounds are hypoactive.
6. An abdominal x-ray reveals three gas shadows in the upper abdomen and a gasless distal abdomen.

1. A 16-month-old girl is brought to the emergency department after falling from a second-story window.
2. Emergency personnel found her unconscious with slow, irregular breathing and intubated her on the scene.
3. Upon arrival, her temperature is 37°C, heart rate is 72 beats per minute, blood pressure is 159/90 mm Hg, and oxygen saturation is 98% while intubated.
4. She remains unconscious, with ecchymosis noted behind the left ear and a visibly deformed distal left upper extremity.

10. Her neurological examination is normal, and she is at the 50th percentile for height and weight.
11. She seems distracted during the interview and responds only intermittently to the physician’s directions.

1. A 57-year-old man presents to the emergency department for shortness of breath.
2. He was riding the train home from a business conference when his symptoms began.
3. The patient has a medical history of obesity, diabetes, diabetic nephropathy, hypertension, and a 40-pack-year smoking history.
4. His current medications include atorvastatin, lisinopril, insulin, metformin, and nicotine gum.
5. His temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 130/87 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 93% on room air.
6. An ECG is ordered as seen in Figure A.
7. A chest radiograph is ordered as seen in Figure B.
8. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below: Serum: Na+: 137 mEq/L Cl-: 105 mEq/L K+: 4.1 mEq/L HCO3-: 24 mEq/L BUN: 22 mg/dL Glucose: 129 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.2 mg/dL Ca2+: 10.1 mg/dL AST: 11 U/L ALT: 12 U/L On physical exam, the patient appears to be in distress.
9. His cardiac exam is notable for tachycardia.
10. Pulmonary exam reveals bilateral air movement without any wheezes or crackles.
11. The patient's right lower extremity appears mildly inflamed, and palpation of the calf elicits pain.

1. A 65-year-old woman presents to her family doctor to reestablish care since losing her insurance.
2. She has not had time for regular check-ups.
3. She exercises 3-4 times a week and consumes red meat sparingly.
4. She drank and smoked cigarettes socially with coworkers but never at home or on vacation.
5. She wakes up with achy wrists and elbows that she suspects is from years of using a computer keyboard.
6. She completed menopause at age 52.
7. Her family history is notable for coronary artery disease on her father's side and colon cancer on her mother's side.
8. She last had a colonoscopy 5 years ago that revealed no abnormal findings.
9. Her temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 125/83 mmHg, pulse is 82/min, respirations are 12/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air.
10. Her physical exam is grossly unremarkable.

1. A 66-year-old man is evaluated for a 9-month history of altered bowel habits and recent blood in his stool.  
2. His medical history includes hypertension managed with lisinopril.  
3. Vital signs include a blood pressure of 134/90 mm Hg, heart rate of 78/min, respiratory rate of 14/min, and temperature of 37.5°C (99.5°F).  
4. On examination, the patient appears anxious, and a palpable mass is detected in the left lower quadrant of the abdomen.  
5. Colonoscopy reveals a neoplasm in the descending colon, and biopsy confirms colorectal cancer.

1. A 23-year-old male presents to the emergency department with acute testicular pain that began 15 minutes prior and has not subsided.
2. His medical history is unremarkable, and he is not taking any medications.
3. Vital signs include a temperature of 98.5°F (36.9°C), blood pressure of 123/62 mmHg, pulse of 124/min, respirations of 18/min, and oxygen saturation of 98% on room air.
4. Physical examination reveals a non-tender abdomen, a right testicle positioned higher than the left in a horizontal orientation, and an absent cremasteric reflex upon stroking the medial thigh.

1. An 8-week-old boy presents with his mother to the pediatrician for a well visit.
2. The patient has been breastfed since birth, and usually feeds for 30 minutes every 2-3 hours.
3. The patient’s mother is concerned that her milk production is not keeping up with the patient’s nutritional requirements.
4. She reports that about 2 weeks ago the patient began regurgitating breastmilk through his nose and mouth after some feeds.
5. He seems mildly upset during the episodes of regurgitation but usually settles down quickly and is hungry again soon afterwards.
6. His mother has already tried limiting the volume of each feed, which seems to have reduced the frequency of regurgitation.
7. She denies any diarrhea, hematochezia, or family history of food allergies.
8. Her older son had a similar problem with vomiting that resolved around 12 months of age.
9. Four weeks ago, the patient’s height and weight were in the 40th and 34th percentiles, respectively.
10. His height and weight are now respectively in the 37th and 36th percentiles.
11. His temperature is 98.6°F (37°C), blood pressure is 72/49 mmHg, pulse is 121/min, and respirations are 32/min.
12. On physical exam, the patient is cooing in his mother’s lap and smiles reciprocally with her.
13. He lifts his head and shoulders off the examination table when placed in the supine position.
14. His abdomen is soft, non-tender and non-distended.
15. Bowel sounds are normoactive.

1. A 5-year-old boy is brought to the clinic with a 1-day history of fever and irritability.  
2. His mother notes that he has been frequently pulling at his right ear.  
3. The child recently began attending a new day care center.  
4. His mother denies any respiratory, rash, or gastrointestinal symptoms.  
5. His temperature is 38.0°C (100.4°F).  
6. On examination, the right tympanic membrane appears red, bulging, and has limited mobility.  
7. A Chapman reflex point is also noted superior to the right clavicle.

1. A 50-year-old female with a history of chronic alcohol use disorder presents with severe abdominal pain.
2. Her medical history includes peptic ulcer disease.
3. Physical examination is challenging as the patient refuses abdominal palpation due to the intensity of the pain.
4. The provider suspects spontaneous bacterial peritonitis.

1. A 15-year-old girl is brought to the clinic because her mother is worried the patient has not yet had her period.
2. The patient’s older sister had her first period at age 14.
3. The mother had her first period at age 13.
4. The patient reports she is doing well in school and is on the varsity basketball team.
5. Her medical history is significant for asthma and atopic dermatitis.
6. Her medications include albuterol and topical triamcinolone.
7. Her temperature is 98°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 111/72 mmHg, pulse is 65/min, and respirations are 14/min with an oxygen saturation of 99% on room air.
8. Her body mass index (BMI) is 19 kg/m^2.
9. Physical exam shows absent breast development and external genitalia at Tanner stage 1.
10. Serum follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) level is measured to be 38 mIU/mL.

1. An 8-year-old boy was seen by friends falling into a warm lake during the summer.
2. He was pulled out 6 minutes later by nearby adults, who contacted emergency medical services (EMS).
3. Upon EMS arrival, the boy was unresponsive and pulseless.
4. He underwent cardiopulmonary resuscitation, oral intubation, and intraosseous needle placement.
5. Epinephrine was administered via the endotracheal tube and intraosseous infusion, followed by a 20 mL/kg fluid bolus through intraosseous infusion.
6. After 15 minutes, spontaneous circulation returned.

1. A 67-year-old man presents to the emergency department 1 hour after sudden-onset weakness and double vision.
2. His medical history is significant for hyperlipidemia and poorly controlled hypertension.
3. His current medications include atorvastatin and amlodipine.
4. His temperature is 98.6°F (37.0°C), blood pressure is 175/95 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 16/min.
5. On cranial nerve exam, his left pupil is 6 mm in diameter compared to 3 mm on the right.
6. His left eye is displaced laterally and downward and he also has left-sided ptosis.
7. Strength is 2/5 in the right upper and right lower extremities and 5/5 in the left upper and left lower extremities.
8. He has marked right-sided dysdiadochokinesia.
9. Sensation is intact throughout.

1. A 65-year-old male patient seeks medical attention for episodes of retrosternal pain and dyspnea occurring over the past 10 days.
2. These symptoms manifest during stair climbing or brisk treadmill walking and subside with rest.
3. The previous night, he experienced dizziness and weakness during one such episode.
4. He reports having had a cold 2 weeks prior.
5. His medical history includes type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed 4 years ago, managed with glyburide.
6. Physical examination reveals a well-appearing patient with a weak pulse of 62/min, respiratory rate of 20/min, and blood pressure of 134/90 mm Hg.
7. A late systolic ejection murmur is detected at the second right intercostal space during cardiovascular examination.
8. Lung auscultation is normal.

1. A 74-year-old woman was referred for bilateral blurry vision occurring 2 hours after a car crash.
2. At the moment of impact, she was wearing her seat belt, the airbag deployed, and an intense flexion-extension head movement occurred.
3. Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/125 OD and 20/63 OS.
4. Intraocular pressure was 19 mm Hg OD and 20 mm Hg OS.
5. Slitlamp examination revealed no palpebral hematoma, and the anterior segment was found to be normal.
6. On the fundus bilaterally, we only noted an alteration of the foveal reflection, with neither retinae commotio nor hemorrhages.
7. Macular optical coherence tomography (OCT) showed bilateral macular edema with cystoid abnormalities (Figure 1).
8. An epiretinal membrane also was noted in the left eye (Figure 1B).
9. Optical coherence tomography showed bilateral macular edema with cystoid abnormalities.
10. Central subfield thickness was 696 μm in the right eye and 392 μm in the left eye.

1. A 42-year-old woman comes to the clinic with a one-month history of low back pain.
2. She denies any recent trauma and works as a journalist, spending most of her time seated at a desk.
3. On examination in the prone position, there is a deep sacral sulcus on the right and a posterior inferior lateral angle (ILA) on the left.
4. During a seated forward bend test, the left posterior superior iliac spine (PSIS) moves superiorly.
5. L5 is noted to be flexed, rotated to the right, and sidebent to the right.

1. A young boy aged 6 is evaluated by a physician due to academic difficulties lasting one year.  
2. His history reveals early speech problems, sensory sensitivities (refusing to wear shoes), repetitive hand movements, and heightened sound sensitivity.  
3. According to his teacher, he plays in isolation, arranging toy trucks in lines.  
4. His medical record notes functional constipation treated with polyethylene glycol as needed.  
5. Growth parameters show height at 60th percentile, weight at 55th percentile, and head circumference at 88th percentile.  
6. During examination, he shows some ability to engage with objects the physician indicates but uses gestures rather than speech and avoids direct verbal responses.  
7. Both hearing and vision are normal.

1. A woman in her 70s presented with an enlarged and variegated plaque on her left axilla, which she had had for 4 years.
2. The lesion started as a small eczematous, pink-to-brown plaque.
3. As the lesion was asymptomatic and slow growing, she did not initially seek treatment.
4. Recently, the color of the lesion had changed to an alarming dark brown color (Figure, A).
5. No breast mass or lymphadenopathy was observed.
6. Her medical and family history was unremarkable.
7. A skin biopsy specimen was obtained and submitted for further histopathologic analysis.A, Clinical presentation of pigmented plaque in the axilla with well-demarcated margins.
8. B, Histologic findings revealed an intraepidermal neoplasm consisting of pagetoid cells, characterized by round, pale, vacuolated cytoplasm, and large pleomorphic nuclei (hematoxylin-eosin; original magnification ×200).
9. C, Immunohistochemical findings showed positive staining for EMA (original magnification ×200).
10. D, The lesion was surrounded by numerous reactive dendritic HMB-45–positive melanocytes scattered among the tumor cells (original magnification ×200).

1. Patient D is a 27-year-old  male presenting with several days of right leg pain since doing a session at the gym
2. Patient D describes the pain as starting in his lower back and radiating down the side and back of his right leg all the way to his foot
3. Patient D describes some paresthesias of his right foot during physical examination, but he has full strength and sensation intact to light touch
4. An MRI of his lumbar spine reveals a disk herniation at L5-S1 impinging on his right L5 nerve root
5. Patient D's pain is now so severe he is having difficulty ambulating.

1. Patient D is a 62-year-old  male who is post-op day 3 status-post bi-frontal craniotomy for resection of an olfactory groove meningioma
2. Surgery was uncomplicated, and he has been healing well with no new deficits beyond expected loss of smell
3. Patient D is meeting all milestones for discharge, however he continues to have significant head pain at the site of his craniotomy
4. During your pre-discharge physical examination, you note that there is expected frontal scalp swelling and tenderness to palpation of his incision site
5. You review the medication administration record and see that he has required 1 dose of hydrocodone every 6 hours for pain control.

1. A female patient in her early 50s presented with multiple (approximately 10) bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs (Figure, A).
2. Since the age of 24 years, the lesions had been growing very slowly in number and size and had been bleeding occasionally after a trauma.
3. The patient used a wheelchair due to a right-sided hemiparesis and hemianopsia caused by an intracranial hemorrhage.
4. At the age of 4 years, recurrent seizures had led to the diagnosis of cerebral venous malformations.
5. Clinical examination also demonstrated a lipolymphedema of the lower legs that had been attributed to a functional venous insufficiency with insufficient venous pump activity.
6. The patient had been wearing compression stockings for years.
7. The family history was positive for cerebral venous malformations involving the patient’s father and aunt, the father having died of an intracranial hemorrhage in his early 70s.A, Clinical picture.
8. B and C, Hematoxylin-eosin stain.Sonography of the skin lesions demonstrated intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations with a maximum diameter of 1.2 cm.
9. A biopsy of a lower-extremity papule was performed (Figure, B and C).
10. Mutational analysis resulted in the detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant.

1. A 73-year-old man with a 2- to 3-week history of herpes zoster in the left T11-T12 dermatomes developed a painful, progressive bulge in his left flank.
2. The bulge was more prominent on standing, coughing, and straining.
3. Antiviral agents were not administered when he first developed zoster because the diagnosis was established more than 72 hours after first presentation of the disease.
4. Neither fever nor chills were reported.
5. The patient’s medical history was notable for a 30-year history of hypertension and diabetes.
6. Physical examination revealed a reducible protrusion in the left flank, with several red to light brown macules on the overlying skin (Figure).
7. Computed tomography (CT) of the abdomen showed convexity of the left lower abdominal wall compared with the right and did not reveal any mass, hernia, or accumulation of fluid in the abdominal cavity.A, Lateral view showing hyperpigmented macules on the overlying skin of the left flank bulge.
8. B, Posterior view showing the left flank protrusion.Proceed with expectant treatment over the next few months

1. A 49-year-old man presents to the emergency department with 3 days of pain and redness of the skin on his right lower leg.  
2. He has had type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 12 years, and is only intermittently adherent to his medication regimen.  
3. He has smoked 10–15 cigarettes per day for the past 20 years.  
4. His temperature is 38°C (100.4°F), pulse is 95/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg.  
5. On physical examination, the right pretibial area is erythematous, edematous, and tender.  
6. He is diagnosed with acute cellulitis and therapy with intravenous ceftriaxone is initiated.  
7. On the 5th day of the antibiotic therapy, the patient is noted to have severe watery diarrhea, a temperature of 38.2 °C (100.8°F), and abdominal tenderness without rigidity.  
8. A complete blood count shows 14,000 WBCs/mm3, and his serum creatinine is 1.1 mg/dL.

1. A woman in her 30s presented with progressive, multiple itchy erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques localized to the left shin for more than 10 years (Figure, A and B).
2. On close inspection, milia and a few erosions with partially detached epidermis were identified.
3. There were no abnormalities of the mucous membranes, nails, hair, or teeth.
4. No extracutaneous involvement was observed.A, Multiple pruritic erythematous to violaceous lichenified papules and plaques on the left shin.
5. B, Close-up of the skin lesions showing an erosion with partially detached epidermis and multiple milia.
6. C, Histopathologic examination revealed dermoepidermal separation (hematoxylin-eosin stain).
7. D, Histopathologic examination revealed several milia (hematoxylin-eosin stain).

1. A 72-year-old man seeks medical attention for urinary difficulties lasting 6 months, characterized by slow and intermittent urinary stream with terminal dribbling.
2. He reports no blood in urine or painful urination.
3. His medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, managed with lisinopril and atorvastatin.
4. Vital signs show: pulse 72/min, respiratory rate 14/min, blood pressure 140/92 mm Hg, and temperature 36.8°C (98.3°F).
5. The patient is alert and oriented.
6. Cardiac examination reveals a 2/6 systolic murmur at the left sternal border and an S3 gallop.
7. Digital rectal examination finds a symmetrically enlarged, non-tender prostate without nodules.
8. Stool occult blood test is negative.

1. A 41-year-old woman presents with right hip pain that began a week ago after making an unusual step, resulting in immediate dull pain in the right hip.
2. She rates the pain as 6/10, describing it as achy and non-radiating.
3. The pain worsens when stretching her right quadriceps and is partially alleviated by NSAIDs.
4. Physical examination reveals a slight reduction in hip extension range of motion, with 5/5 strength bilaterally in both lower extremities.
5. A discrete, non-radiating tender point is identified just medial to the right anterior superior iliac spine.

1. A 45-year-old woman with systemic sclerosis (scleroderma) comes to the physician because of a 3-week history of progressive shortness of breath and nonproductive cough.  
2. Her temperature is 36.9°C (98.4°F), pulse is 82/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 136/85 mm Hg.  
3. Crackles are heard in both lower lung fields.  
4. Pulmonary function tests show total lung capacity is 80% of predicted, and diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide, corrected for alveolar volume, is 65% of predicted.

1. A woman in her early 50s with a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, diabetes, stroke, and coronary artery disease that required coronary artery bypass graft 6 years earlier presented to the emergency department with 12 hours of sudden-onset, constant, right lower quadrant abdominal pain associated with vomiting and melena.
2. She denied any hematochezia or history of peptic ulcer disease.
3. She had no other surgical history and denied alcohol use or smoking.
4. On examination, she was hypertensive (blood pressure, 185/85 mm Hg) although not tachycardic and was afebrile.
5. She was locally tender to palpation in the right lower quadrant with rebound and voluntary guarding.
6. Her abdomen was not tympanitic.
7. The patient had no abdominal scars, hernias, or palpable masses.
8. Laboratory results were significant for the following: leukocyte count, 23 600/µL (to convert to ×109/L, multiply by 0.001) with neutrophilia (94%); blood urea nitrogen level, 28 mg/dL (to convert to millimoles per liter, multiply by 0.357); creatinine concentration, 0.01 mg/dL (to convert to micromoles per liter, multiply by 88.4); lipase concentration, 195 U/L (to convert to microkatals per liter, multiply by 0.0167); and lactate concentration, 2.02 mg/dL (to convert to millimoles per liter, multiply by 0.111).
9. Electrolyte levels and liver function test results were within normal limits.
10. An electrocardiogram showed normal sinus rhythm.
11. Computed tomography of the abdomen and pelvis with oral and intravenous contrast enhancement was performed (Figure).
12. Axial cross-sectional computed tomograms of the patient’s abdomen and pelvis with oral and intravenous contrast enhancement show segmental mural thickening of the anterior cecum with wall hypoenhancement and pneumatosis, adjacent fat stranding, and a lucency medial to the cecum (A) and bilateral renal hypodensities (B).

1. A 64-year-old female presents to the emergency department following a fall, resulting in a right distal radius fracture.
2. Initial testing reveals a serum sodium of 128 mEq/liter.
3. Her medical conditions include hypertension, hypothyroidism, osteoporosis, and depression, managed with lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, levothyroxine 100 μg daily, sertraline 100 mg daily, and alendronate 70 mg weekly.
4. She is alert and oriented, with normal vital signs and physical examination findings except for her casted right forearm.

1. A 37-year-old man comes to the physician because of nonradiating low back pain for 3 days.
2. The pain began after he worked in his yard.
3. He has not had any change in bowel movements or urination.
4. He had one similar episode 3 years ago that resolved spontaneously.
5. Vital signs are within normal limits.
6. Examination of the back shows bilateral paravertebral muscle spasm.
7. Range of motion is limited by pain.
8. Straight-leg raising is negative.

1. Patient D is a 75-year-old  male with history of lung cancer and 4 months of progressive low-back and right leg pain
2. Patient D describes the pain as a dull ache that shoots down his right leg in no particular pattern or frequency
3. Recently, he started experiencing intermittent numbness throughout his right leg
4. Overall, he believes the pain is becoming more frequent and intolerable, as it now interrupts his sleep nightly and acetaminophen and ibuprofen have not helped
5. On your physical examination, you find that Patient D has diffusely diminished sensation in his leg, but his strength and reflexes are normal
6. Upon reviewing his lumbar spine MRI, you identify diffuse leptomeningeal disease
7.

1. A man in his 60s with a medical history of hypertension, cerebrovascular accident, colon cancer, and remote cocaine use presented with numerous pruritic crusted papules and nodules on the face and genitals.  
2. The eruption presented abruptly over a 2-week course, and the patient attributed it to contact with plants while working in his yard.  
3. He denied having similar lesions in the past.  
4. He had used over-the-counter topical antibiotic and antihistamine creams, which alleviated the pruritus.  
5. He denied recent sexual intercourse, penile discharge, fevers, chills, nausea, or vomiting.  
6. Physical examination of the bilateral cheeks, glabella, dorsal nose, and chin revealed multiple skin-colored papules, nodules, and vegetative plaques ranging in size from 4 to 6 mm in diameter, with central umbilication, erosions, and overlying yellow crust (Figure, A).  
7. There were similar lesions on the scrotum and inner thighs, with sparing of the penis (Figure, B).  
8. There was also a 1-cm ulceration on the left lower lip.  
9. The palms and soles were spared.  
10. There was no lymphadenopathy noted.  
11. One 4-mm punch biopsy specimen was obtained from a nodule on the left medial cheek, bisectioned, and sent for both hematoxylin–eosin staining and tissue cultures for bacteria, fungi, and atypical mycobacteria (Figure, C and D).  
12. A, Multiple crusted and ulcerative papules and nodules on the face.  
13. B, Multiple ulcerated healing papules on the scrotum and umbilicated papules on the left inner thigh.  
14. C, Low-power image (hematoxylin-eosin, original magnification ×40).  
15. D, A Warthin-Starry silver impregnation stain (original magnification ×40).

1. A 47-year-old man presents with fatigue and reduced libido.
2. Over the past year, he has experienced a decline in sexual interest, infrequent morning erections, and only mild erections during masturbation.
3. He occasionally has morning headaches.
4. He reports no loss of axillary or pubic hair, no history of testicular trauma, and no mumps infection.
5. Puberty occurred normally.
6. He is divorced and has two healthy children, ages 15 and 17.
7. His BMI is 38.
8. Physical examination reveals normal axillary and pubic hair.
9. Both testicles measure approximately 10 cc (reference range: 15–25).
10. Visual field testing is normal.

1. An 18-year-old girl presents to clinic for her first well-woman visit.  
2. She has no complaints currently.  
3. Menarche was at age 13, and her last menses was 2 weeks ago.  
4. Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 110/60 mmHg, pulse is 84/min, and respirations are 15/min.  
5. Her physical exam, including pelvic exam, is normal.  
6. She currently takes no medications and has no allergies.  
7. She denies illicit drug use and acknowledges that she is sexually active.

1. A 19-year-old male presents with a 4-week history of recurrent headaches.  
2. He denies any history of head trauma but mentions experiencing increased stress at school, which worsens the headaches.  
3. On physical examination, the patient appears comfortable, and cranial nerves II-XII are intact.  
4. During an osteopathic structural exam, while performing the vault hold, you note that the left greater wing of the sphenoid is positioned more superiorly compared to the right.

1. A 27-year-old female presents with a generalized rash of 5 days' duration, accompanied by mild fever, headache, and muscle aches over the past month.
2. She has no significant medical history.
3. Her social history includes smoking one pack of cigarettes daily, weekend binge drinking, and occasional cocaine use.
4. Her vital signs are normal.
5. Physical findings include a widespread, symmetric, reddish-brown papular rash on her trunk, upper extremities, and palms, along with generalized non-tender lymphadenopathy.
6. She also exhibits patchy scalp alopecia and multiple flat, broad-based, wartlike papules in the anogenital region.
7. Both rapid plasma reagin and fluorescent treponemal antibody tests are positive.

1. A man in his 80s presented with a 1-year history of purpura, ecchymoses, anorexia, and weight loss.
2. His medical history included alcohol abuse and cognitive impairment.
3. Purpura and ecchymoses, initially periorbital, progressed over the previous 12 months.
4. Elder abuse was excluded.
5. Examination demonstrated waxy yellow papules and plaques with purpura in the periocular, neck, axillary, trunk, and inguinal regions (Figure, A).
6. Investigations revealed anemia, abnormal liver function test results, and renal impairment with moderate proteinuria.
7. The patient’s serum protein electrophoresis (SPEP) and immunofixation urine protein electrophoresis test results were normal.
8. Radiological studies were unremarkable.
9. Subsequently, a 4-mm punch biopsy specimen was obtained (Figure, B-D).
10. A, Waxy yellow discoloration of the skin with papules and purpura in the periorbital region.
11. B, Punch biopsy specimen (hematoxylin-eosin, original magnification × 4).
12. C, Punch biopsy specimen stained with Congo red (original magnification × 10).
13. D, Punch biopsy specimen under polarized microscopy (original magnification × 10).

1. A 66-year-old woman with chronic hepatitis B infection and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) presented with subacute epigastric pain.
2. Three years prior, she was diagnosed with a solitary HCC and underwent surgical resection with curative intent.
3. Pathology revealed poorly differentiated HCC, 16 cm in largest dimension, with large vein involvement (T3bNXM0, R0 resection).
4. The patient underwent expectant observation.
5. One and a half years prior to the current presentation, laboratory results revealed an elevated α-fetoprotein (AFP), and cross-sectional imaging revealed multiple lung nodules consistent with metastases.
6. She was treated with nivolumab every other week and attained a biochemical (baseline, 212.2 ng/dL; best response, 3.3 ng/dL) and radiographic complete response.In the current presentation, the patient reported nonradiating epigastric pain of moderate intensity for 1 month.
7. Associated symptoms included nausea, anorexia, and water brash without emesis.
8. Review of systems was positive for unchanged chronic abdominal bloating and negative for other constitutional or gastrointestinal symptoms.
9. Laboratory results, including liver function tests, amylase, lipase, and AFP, were within normal limits, and hepatitis B virus polymerase chain reaction was undetectable.
10. Computed tomography with multiphasic liver protocol showed new enlarged mesenteric nodes and diffuse thickening of the gastric body (Figure, A).
11. Esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) identified diffuse inflammation and ulcerations in the gastric body and antrum (Figure, B).
12. Biopsy specimens showed chronic and active mixed inflammatory infiltrate, including intraepithelial lymphocytosis (Figure, C).
13. No overt viral cytopathic effects were observed, and immunostaining results for Helicobacter pylori, cytomegalovirus, and adenovirus were negative.A, Coronal view of restaging computed tomography of chest, abdomen, and pelvis with contrast.
14. The yellow circle notes borderline enlarged mesenteric nodes inferior to the stomach, and the yellow arrowheads show thickened gastric body wall.
15. B, Gross appearance of the gastric mucosa visualized via upper endoscopy, which showed diffuse inflammation and ulceration in the gastric body and antrum.
16. C, Biopsy of the gastric mucosa showed marked chronic and active intraepithelial infiltration of lymphocytes (blue arrowheads) and neutrophils (yellow arrowhead) and associated glandular epithelial injury with withered glands and gland dropout (red circle) (original magnification ×100).

1. A 52-year-old female presents to the office with the complaint of greenish discharge from her left nipple.
2. There is no history of trauma or fever, and the patient is not currently using oral contraceptives nor is she on hormone replacement therapy.
3. Her last pregnancy was approximately 20 years ago.
4. Physical examination findings are normal except for the green discharge.

1. An 84-year-old woman with a 5-year history of Alzheimer disease is brought in by her family for evaluation of worsening symptoms, including memory loss, wandering, and a decline in her ability to perform daily activities.  
2. She has been on donepezil for the past year, which initially provided noticeable improvement in her symptoms.  
3. However, her family is now uncertain if the medication is still benefiting her.

1. A 69-year-old man presents to clinic due to shortness of breath, worsening pain in his right shoulder, and episodes of hemoptysis.
2. His symptoms began 3 months ago.
3. He has also lost 18 pounds.
4. He has a history of coronary artery disease and underwent an uncomplicated coronary angioplasty with stent placement 2 years ago.
5. He routinely travels both domestically and internationally as a senior shipyard worker and has a 30-pack-year smoking history.
6. He used to drink 4 cocktails a week.
7. He has not smoke or drank alcohol in over 7 years.
8. His temperature is 99.5°F (37.7°C), blood pressure is 140/60 mmHg, pulse is 97/min, and respirations are 13/min.
9. Physical exam is notable for right pupillary constriction as well as paresthesias in his right fourth and fifth digits.
10. There is no pain with active shoulder rotation.
11. His chest imaging is shown in Figure A.

1. Patient D is a 52-year-old  male with hepatitis C and cirrhosis who presents with new abdominal pain
2. Patient D was preparing breakfast when he had sudden onset of sharp pain in his right upper abdomen
3. Patient D denies any nausea or vomiting, but he feels the pain worse with inspiration and is in severe discomfort

1. A pregnant woman in her late 30s had normal findings on anatomic ultrasonography at 19 weeks’ gestation.  
2. Follow-up ultrasonography at 32 weeks’ gestation identified fetal hydrops.  
3. The fetal ultrasonogram showed a large left-sided hydrothorax, mediastinal shift, and ascites.  
4. After ruling out infectious causes, an ultrasonography-guided thoracoamniotic shunt was placed successfully at 32 weeks’ gestation.  
5. Results of follow-up ultrasonography on postoperative day 3 showed improvement in the fetal hydrothorax and resolution of hydrops and identified a feeding vessel originating from the descending aorta supplying a lung mass (Figure 1A).  
6. A, Feeding vessel (arrowhead) from descending aorta identified on ultrasonography at 32 weeks’ gestation.  
7. B, Feeding vessel (arrowhead) to lung mass (outlined) over left hemidiaphragm on computed tomography at age 9 months.  
8. Owing to premature rupture of membranes, the mother delivered at 33 weeks.  
9. The neonate showed no respiratory distress after birth, and the shunt was removed.  
10. On the day of birth, radiographic findings showed a left-sided pleural effusion.  
11. Ongoing pleural effusion caused respiratory distress, and on day 3 of life, a temporary thoracostomy tube was placed.  
12. During the following weeks, the thoracostomy tube output decreased, the tube was removed, and the patient was discharged home.  
13. At 9 months of age, follow-up computed tomography confirmed a lung mass with a feeding vessel (Figure 1B), and the patient returned for elective thoracoscopic resection.

1. A 20-year-old woman comes to the primary care clinic with complaints of a progressively worsening sore throat, dry cough, and ear pain.

6. Chest auscultation is unremarkable, but a chest X-ray reveals bilateral multifocal opacities in the lungs.
7. Sputum culture and Gram stain are negative.

1. A 60-year-old man with an 8-year history of moderate rheumatoid arthritis presents with worsening pain and swelling in both wrists lasting over a week.

1. A 28-year-old man presented with abdominal pain and diarrhea (10-12 Bristol type 7 stools per day; Bristol scale range, 1-7 [1, separate hard pieces; 7, watery stool]) after completing a course of azithromycin for pneumonia.  
2. He was diagnosed with Clostridium difficile infection (CDI) with a positive stool polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for the toxin B (tcdB) gene.

6. Vital signs and physical examination were unremarkable and a repeat stool test for C difficile toxin PCR was positive.

1. A 47-year-old male visits his primary care physician reporting a seven-month history of fatigue.

1. A 14-year-old boy is brought to the physician for a physical examination prior to participating in sports.

1. A 57-year-old woman comes to the physician because of an 8-week history of difficulty sleeping, fatigue, and muscle tension.

1. A teenage girl presented with recurrent episodes of palpitations for 6 consecutive years.  
2. The resting 12-lead electrocardiogram showed sinus rhythm with no preexcitation or repolarization abnormalities.  
3. There were incessant multiple runs of nonsustained ventricular tachycardia with right bundle branch block morphologic features.  
4. QRS complexes were negative in the rest of the precordial leads (V2-V6) and in leads I and avL, but positive in III, avR, and avF, suggesting a left (lateral) ventricular apical origin (Figure 1).  
5. The echocardiogram showed no structural abnormalities.  
6. The patient was prescribed sotalol but her symptoms did not improve.  
7. Invasive electrophysiological mapping of the left ventricle endocardium demonstrated that the ventricular tachycardia probably originated from the epicardial surface of left ventricular apex.Twelve-lead surface electrocardiogram during tachycardia.  
8. QRS complexes are positive in V1, negative in the rest of the precordial leads (V2-V6), and negative in leads I and avL but positive in III, avR, and avF.Add a second antiarrhythmic drug and reassess the need for epicardial intervention after 3 to 6 monthsPerform cardiac magnetic resonance imaging to define pathologic substrate

1. A 15-year-old girl comes to the emergency department because, she says, "something has been sticking out of my bottom since I had a bowel movement this morning." She has not had previous episodes, although for more than 1 year she has had occasional difficulty passing stools.

1. A 56-year-old male patient presents with severe right leg pain and swelling four days after undergoing a craniotomy with evacuation of a subdural hematoma.

1. An elderly male patient, aged 87, resides in a subacute nursing facility with a medical history significant for Parkinson disease and stroke.

5. Tuning fork testing, performed after hearing aid removal, shows Weber test lateralization to the right side, and bilateral positive Rinne tests (air conduction superior to bone conduction).
6. The remainder of his neurological examination is unremarkable.

1. A 28-year-old woman visited the emergency department for a sudden, diffuse, and painful enlargement of the upper quadrants of the left breast with edema and palpable axillary lymph nodes without clinical signs of inflammation or infection (Figure 1A).

3. Initial presentation of the patient.
4. A, Asymmetric mass in the upper quadrant of the left breast.
5. B, Breast ultrasonogram revealing hypoechogenicity of the breast tissue with periductal small cysts.
6. The patient had stopped breastfeeding 10 months before the emergency department admission, and she had a recent history of pneumonia self-medicated with antibiotics.
7. She had no family history of breast or ovarian cancer and no history of drug addiction or hyaluronic acid or free silicone injections in the breast.
8. She denied any trauma to the breast.
9. On physical examination, the patient had a 6-cm hard mass without nipple discharge or retraction and left axillary palpable lymph nodes.
10. Breast ultrasonography revealed diffuse nonspecific hypoechogenicity of the breast tissue with periductal small cysts (Figure 1B).

14. Blood test results were as follows: hepatitis B surface antigen, hepatitis C antibody, human immunodeficiency virus enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and whole-blood interferon γ release assay (QuantiFERON), negative; IgG cytomegalovirus, positive; fibrinogen level, 234 mg/dL (to convert to micromoles per liter, multiply by 0.0294); erythrocyte sedimentation rate, 4 mm/h; leukocyte count, 7660/µL (to convert to ×109/L, multiply by 0.001); no acquired immunosuppression; and no hematologic disorders.

9. Suggest supportive strategies (eg, cold compresses, ocular lubricants) and consider increasing the topical corticosteroid treatment or prescribing a topical nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) Prescribe an oral NSAID and/or systemic immunosuppression (oral corticosteroid) and perform chest radiography, urinalysis, blood tests, and other studies Perform a general examination (for a port-wine stain) and dilated ophthalmoscopy

1. A 52-year-old man is admitted to the hospital because of severe dyspnea and cough productive of tenacious, brownishyellow sputum for the past 3 weeks.

1. 1. A 77-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a complaint of sudden onset weakness in his right upper extremity.

1. A man in his 30s presented with a 5-day history of vomiting, followed by lethargy and confusion.
2. Two years prior, he was hospitalized with coma with no identifiable precipitant and an extensive workup done at that time only revealed an elevated ammonia level of 233 µg/dL (to convert to µmol/L, multiply by 0.714); etiology remained unclear but he improved with lactulose.
3. Prior to this admission, he was working in a restaurant, did not ingest any drugs or mushrooms, and had no operations and no family history of similar problems.
4. He was found to have hyperammonemia to 239.5 µg/dL and respiratory alkalosis (pH level, 7.482; partial pressure of carbon dioxide, 27.3 mm Hg, and partial pressure of oxygen, 109 mm Hg [to convert to kPa, multiply by 0.133]; and bicarbonate, 20.2 mEq/L [to convert to mmol/L, multiply by 1]).
5. Liver and kidney function were normal (protein, 6.4 g/dL, and albumin, 3.4 g/dL [to convert to g/L, multiply by 10]; direct bilirubin, 0.1 mg/dL, and indirect bilirubin, 0.8 mg/dL [to convert to µmol/L, multiply by 17.104]; alkaline phosphatase, 38 U/L, aspartate aminotransferase, 22 U/L, and alanine aminotransferase, 42 U/L [to convert to µkat/L, mutiply by 0.0167]).
6. His mental status rapidly declined despite treatment with lactulose, necessitating intubation.
7. Head computed tomography and cerebrospinal fluid analysis were unrevealing.
8. Ammonia levels progressively increased to 1120.5 µg/dL, requiring hemodialysis and sodium phenylbutyrate, which did not lead to significant clinical improvement.
9. On hospital day 6, he developed continuous myoclonus due to status epilepticus (Figure 1A), which was refractory to treatment with lorazepam and levetiracetam as well as continuous midazolam, lorazepam, and propofol infusions.
10. Plasma amino acids and urine organic acids were requested.
11. Continuous venovenous filtration hemodialysis and carnitine treatment were started because of concern for inborn errors of metabolism.
12. Within a few hours of transfer, his ammonia level peaked to 1960 µg/dL and he lost all brainstem activity due to diffuse cerebral edema (Figure 1B).
13. A, Electroencephalography (EEG) showing diffuse polyspike complexes consistent with myoclonic seizures.
14. B, Head computed tomography showing diffuse cerebral edema, obliteration of basal cisterns, and transtentorial and tonsillar herniation.

1. A 19-year-old male presents to the office for evaluation after he was hit from behind below the right knee while playing football.

4. She took no prescription medications; however, she did occasionally take over-the-counter ibuprofen.
5. On examination, she was well-appearing and afebrile.
6. There were tense confluent blisters in a 4-cm area on and around the lower lip (Figure 1) and no other skin or mucosal lesions.

1. A 36-year-old man comes to the office because of headaches that began 2 weeks ago.  
2. The headaches are moderately severe, are present when he awakens in the morning, and are relieved with over-the-counter analgesics.  
3. He has no prior history of headaches.  
4. He tells you he was promoted to an upper-level managerial position in his accounting firm about 8 months ago, which necessitated relocating.  
5. Physical examination now discloses no abnormalities except for blurring of the optic disc margins bilaterally.

1. An 18-year-old female presents to the office with a 3-day history of lower abdominal pain and a 2-day history of fever.
2. She reports frequent unprotected sexual intercourse with different partners since she started college 4 months ago.
3. Abdominal examination reveals suprapubic tenderness.
4. Bimanual examination of the uterus reveals more intense tenderness.
5. Swabs of cervical mucus are obtained.

1. A 79-year-old male is brought to the physician by his daughter due to concerns about memory loss.
2. He previously worked in finance but now needs assistance managing his bills.
3. One month ago, he became lost in his own neighborhood and was unable to find his way home.
4. His vital signs are normal.
5. Neurocognitive testing reveals that he is alert and oriented to person and place but cannot recall the current year or month.
6. During the evaluation, the physician names three unrelated objects clearly and slowly, then immediately asks the patient to repeat the names of all three objects.

1. A 53-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 6-month history of intermittent blood in his stool.
2. He has had no pain with defecation.
3. Physical examination shows a 1-cm, visible anal mass located below the dentate line.
4. A biopsy of the mass is scheduled.

1. A 64-year-old man presented with concern about an abnormal genetic test result for apolipoprotein E (APOE) obtained through his primary care physician.
2. He reported forgetfulness and word-finding difficulties for 3 years but performed all activities of daily living independently and was generally healthy.
3. His father and maternal great aunt developed dementia in their 70s.
4. Physical (including neurologic) examination, basic laboratory studies, and brain magnetic resonance imaging results were normal.
5. The Short Test of Mental Status (STMS) score was 33 (maximal attainable score of 38 indicates best performance).
6. Neuropsychological assessment showed average to above-average performance in all cognitive domains, accounting for age and education.
7. Results of his genetic testing for APOE were reported as follows: “This individual possesses an apolipoprotein E genotype (3 and 4) that indicates, with high specificity, that Alzheimer’s disease is the cause of or a contributor to the observed dementia.”

1. An 8-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of a progressive swelling of her neck for the past 6 months.  
2. She has no pain, dyspnea, or dysphagia.  
3. She is at the 60th percentile for height and the 55th percentile for weight.  
4. Vital signs are within normal limits.  
5. Examination shows a 3-cm cystic, nontender swelling in the midline of the neck.  
6. The swelling moves upwards with protrusion of the tongue.  
7. There is no cervical lymphadenopathy.  
8. Her serum thyroid-stimulating hormone level is 2.1 μU/mL.

1. A newborn boy is evaluated 30 minutes after birth.
2. He was born at 39 weeks gestation to a 27-year-old primigravid mother via cesarean section for cervical insufficiency.
3. The pregnancy was complicated by gestational diabetes and the amniotic fluid was clear.
4. Upon delivery, the patient had strong respiratory effort and a strong cry.

6. The patient now is exhibiting increased work of breathing and is progressively more tachypneic.
