8. His temperature is 99.0°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 60/44 mmHg, pulse is 146/min, and respirations are 72/min.
9. On physical exam, the patient is grunting with nasal flaring and subcostal retractions.
10. Breath sounds are decreased at the bases bilaterally.
11. The patient has central cyanosis.
12. His chest radiograph can be seen in Figure A.

1. A newborn boy is evaluated in the hospital nursery 2 hours after birth.
2. The patient was born at 39 weeks of gestation to a 30-year-old primigravid via vaginal delivery.
3. The patient’s mother received routine prenatal care and the pregnancy was uncomplicated.
4. The patient’s anatomy ultrasound at 20 weeks of gestation was unremarkable.
5. The patient’s mother denies any family history of genetic diseases.
6. The patient’s APGAR scores were notable for poor muscle tone at both 1 and 5 minutes of life.
7. The patient’s birth weight is 2.6 kg (5 lb 11 oz), which is at the 5th percentile.
8. His height and head circumference are in the 15th and 3rd percentile, respectively.
9. His temperature is 97.1°F (36.2°C), blood pressure is 57/42 mmHg, pulse is 140/min, and respirations are 38/min.
10. On physical exam, the patient has a wide nasal bridge, down slanting palpebral fissures, and widely spaced eyes.
11. He has good respiratory effort with a high-pitched cry.

1. A 54-year-old man presents to the clinic with 4 weeks of persistently worsening back pain.
2. The pain is localized to 1 spot in his lower back and is worse with physical activity.
3. His medical history is pertinent for intravenous drug use.
4. He has no past surgical history.
5. His temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F), blood pressure is 118/90 mmHg, pulse is 92/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air.
6. On physical exam, he has midline back tenderness to palpation at L2-L3.
7. Laboratory workup reveals an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 112 mm/h and C-reactive protein of 10 mg/dL.

1. A 68-year-old man presents for evaluation by a neurologist for an involuntary hand tremor that started approximately 3 months ago.
2. The shaking improves when he reaches for objects but returns when he is not using his hand.
3. His temperature is 98.6°F (37.0°C), blood pressure is 115/70 mmHg, pulse is 70/min, and respirations are 12/min.
4. His left hand exhibits a 4-6 Hz tremor when resting on his lap.
5. The tremor extinguishes with voluntary movement.
6. In addition, his left upper extremity has increased tone with passive range of motion.

1. A woman in her mid-30s pregnant with twins at 13 weeks’ gestation presented with a tender right-flank mass, which she noticed after falling and sustaining trauma to the area 1 week previously.
2. Medical history was significant for a total thyroidectomy for papillary thyroid cancer 7 years before as well as a strong family history of malignant breast cancer on the maternal side and colon and liver cancer on the paternal side.
3. Physical examination revealed an 8 × 8-cm, tender, firm posterior right-flank mass that was mobile but fixed to the abdominal wall musculature.
4. Laboratory examination revealed no abnormalities.
5. Ultrasonography demonstrated a hypoechoic lesion measuring 3.3 × 3.6 cm with internal echoes and no significant flow (Figure 1A).
6. A noncontrast magnetic resonance image (MRI) revealed this to be a well-circumscribed T2 hyperintense lesion with diffuse surrounding soft tissue edema within the adjacent muscular and subcutaneous tissues abutting the posterior margin of the right chest wall and external oblique muscle at the level of the T11 to T12 intercostal space (Figure 1B and C).
7. A, Ultrasonography demonstrating a hypoechoic mass in the musculature of the right flank.
8. B and C, T1- and T2-weighted images demonstrating an enhancing right-flank mass within the right-flank musculature.
9. Because of the concern of malignancy, an ultrasonography-guided core biopsy was performed and demonstrated a myofibroblastic proliferation with immunostains positive for actin and negative for S100 and desmin.
10. Her case was presented at the soft tissue tumor board, and given that the patient was asymptomatic and pregnant, the decision was made to closely watch the progression of this lesion with serial imaging with a planned resection after delivery.
11. Unfortunately, she developed premature rupture of membranes and lost the pregnancy.
12. Follow-up computed tomography was not able to identify the lesion but MRI showed that it was still present but decreased in size (2.4 × 1 cm) with interval resolution of surrounding inflammatory changes.
13. She subsequently underwent wide local resection of the lesion.

1. A pregnant woman in her 30s presented at 20 weeks with a 4-week history of bilateral decreased vision.
2. Her medical history was remarkable for type 2 diabetes (which was well-controlled with insulin), and a review of systems found that she had not experienced headache, pain, or neurologic complaints.
3. Her blood pressure was 102/54, and her best-corrected visual acuity was 20/50 OD and 20/40 OS without afferent pupillary defect, motility disturbance, or intraocular pressure abnormalities.
4. A fundus examination was remarkable for bilateral hyperemic discs and macular edema and subretinal fluid, with numerous flame-shaped hemorrhages in 4 quadrants without microaneurysms, exudates, or neovascularization (Figure).
5. There was no evidence of intraocular inflammation.
6. Fluorescein angiography was deferred because of her pregnancy.A and B, Fundus photographs demonstrating macular edema, prominent flame hemorrhages, and a mild tortuosity of the retinal venules.
7. C, Spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (OCT) of the right eye with subretinal fluid and macular edema.
8. Central macular thickness, 1095 μm.A complete blood cell count, antithrombin III, protein C, prothrombin mutation, antiphospholipid, anticardiolipin, diluted Russell viper venom test, and antinuclear antibody testing results were within normal limits.
9. Her protein S level was decreased (61%) and factor V Leiden testing results revealed heterozygosity in the R506Q mutation.

1. A woman in her 80s with a history of nonischemic cardiomyopathy and chronic kidney disease presented with purpuric lesions on her face, elbows, knees, and feet.
2. She was initially admitted for altered mental status in the setting of an unwitnessed fall and was noted to have “bruises” on her lower extremities.
3. Dermatology was consulted after the development of new lesions on her nose, ear, and the extensor surfaces of her arms bilaterally.
4. Admission laboratory test results showed hypercalcemia (calcium level, 11.5 mg/dL) and acute kidney injury (creatinine level, 5.6 mg/dL).
5. On physical examination, the patient’s nose, bilateral cheeks, forehead, and left ear (helical rim and antihelix [Figure, A]) were found to have dusky purpuric macules and patches.
6. Her knees, feet, and the extensor surfaces of her arms had reticulated purpuric macules and patches.
7. There was skin sloughing off the lesions on her elbows (Figure, B) and knees.
8. Four-millimeter punch biopsy specimens were taken from the left ear, right arm, and forehead (Figure, C and D).
9. Clinical and histopathologic images from a case of acral retiform purpura.
10. A, Dusky purpuric macules on the helical rim and antihelix of the ear.
11. B, Reticulated purpuric patches with focal areas of necrosis on the extensor surfaces of the arms.
12. C and D, In specimens from the forehead, multifocal intravascular fibrinoid material consisting of a mix of cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi with relatively little vessel wall inflammation was seen (hematoxylin-eosin, original magnification ×4 [C] and ×10 [D]).

1. A 23-year-old man presents to the emergency department for altered mental status after a finishing a marathon.
2. He has a medical history of obesity and anxiety and is not currently taking any medications.
3. His temperature is 104°F (40°C), blood pressure is 147/88 mmHg, pulse is 200/min, respirations are 33/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air.
4. Physical exam reveals dry mucous membranes, hot flushed skin, and inappropriate responses to the physician's questions.
5. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below.

1. A 63-year-old healthy woman presented with a 3-week history of fluctuating left eye swelling and redness.
2. She also reported a 1-week history of left eye discomfort and left-sided tinnitus and a 1-day history of binocular horizontal diplopia.
3. She denied any history of recent trauma.
4. Ophthalmologic examination at the time revealed visual acuities of 20/30 OD and 20/40 OS.
5. Intraocular pressures were 15 mm Hg OD and 21 mm Hg OS, with a widened pulse pressure of the left eye.
6. Extraocular motility revealed a left eye abduction deficit.
7. Pupils and confrontational visual fields were unremarkable.
8. Hertel measured 16 mm and 17 mm, respectively.
9. Slitlamp examination of the right eye was unremarkable, but examination of the left eye revealed a large subconjunctival hemorrhage and engorged episcleral veins (Figure 1).
10. Fundus examination of both eyes was unremarkable.
11. Clinical photographs taken 3 weeks apart.
12. A, Dilated nasal episcleral vessels and conjunctival chemosis near the onset of the patient’s symptoms.
13. B, Photograph taken 3 weeks later revealing increased dilated episcleral vessels and subconjunctival hemorrhage.
14. Orbital ecchymosis is also evident.

1. A 31-year-old man presents to clinic for evaluation of a 3-year history of infertility.
2. He has no significant medical history and takes no medications.
3. He exercises twice a day, often with heavy weightlifting, and eats a high-protein diet.
4. He reports occasional alcohol use and remote marijuana use.
5. His temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 148/90 mmHg, pulse is 84/min, and respirations are 15/min.
6. He is sexually active with his wife and has no history of sexually transmitted infections.
7. Physical exam reveals small testes and a receding hairline.
8. He also has palpable tissue underneath his nipples bilaterally.
9. His muscle tone is normal in his upper and lower extremities bilaterally.

1. An 81-year-old man arrives at an urgent care center with sudden-onset shortness of breath.
2. He is alert and interactive but unable to provide a detailed medical history, except for a smoking history of one pack per day from age 15 to 60.
3. He is unsure of his medications, as his daughter manages his pillbox, but he denies using inhalers.
4. Over the past week, he has experienced worsening dyspnea, both at rest and during activity.
5. He also has a chronic cough that has recently worsened, producing clear sputum without changes in volume or purulence.
6. Five days ago, his primary care physician prescribed furosemide 40 mg daily, which has not alleviated his symptoms.
7. On examination, his blood pressure is 127/83 mm Hg, heart rate is 89 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation is 92% on room air.
8. Lung auscultation reveals diminished air entry with bilateral crackles at the bases that clear with coughing, along with expiratory wheezing.
9. A cardiac exam identifies a 3/6 holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border, which intensifies with inhalation.
10. His internal jugular venous pressure (JVP) is 11 cm H₂O, rising to 16 cm with abdominal pressure and returning to baseline within 2–3 seconds.
11. His lower extremities show erythema and 1+ pitting edema to the mid-ankle, which the patient reports has been stable for a month.
12. Laboratory results include a serum creatinine level of 0.9 mg/dL (reference range: 0.8–1.3), hemoglobin concentration of 10.2 g/dL (13.5–17.5), and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) level of 1337 pg/mL (10–131).

1. A woman in her late 40s presented with rapidly progressive redness and stiffness of both hands, accompanied by 2 months of multiple finger joint and right shoulder pain.
2. Results of autoimmune serology, including antinuclear antibody, C3 and C4, rheumatoid factor, and Scl-70 antibody tests, were negative.
3. Raynaud phenomenon was not seen.
4. There was an absence of nailfold capillary changes and distal digital pitting.
5. The patient was treated with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, systemic steroid therapy, and disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (ie, hydroxychloroquine), but symptoms persisted.
6. Two weeks after treatment initiation, multiple tender nodules developed over the palms and interphalangeal joints, and flexion contractures continued (Figure, A).
7. Incisional skin biopsy of the palmar nodules (Figure, B and C) and computed tomography (CT) were performed.
8. Results of the CT demonstrated bilateral ovarian tumors with highly suspect peritoneal metastases.
9. A, Clinical image of erythematous and edematous changes of bilateral hands and multiple nodules on palms and interphalangeal joints.
10. B and C, Hematoxylin-eosin–stained specimen showing increased fibroblasts with fibrosis from dermis to subcutis.

1. A 55-year-old man presents to urgent care for weakness and weight loss.
2. For the past several months, he has felt progressively weaker and has lost 25 pounds with intermittent abdominal pain.
3. The patient has not seen a physician in 30 years and recalls being current on most of his vaccinations.
4. A few years ago, he went to the emergency department due to abdominal pain and was found to have increased liver enzymes due to excessive alcohol use and incidental gallstones.
5. The patient has a 50 pack-year smoking history.
6. His temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 161/108 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air.
7. Physical exam reveals an emaciated man.
8. The patient has a negative Murphy sign and his abdomen is non-tender.
9. Cardiopulmonary exam is within normal limits.

1. A 33-year-old woman presents with a 2-year history of inability to conceive despite regular intercourse.  
2. She and her husband have no prior children.  
3. Her husband denies any history of chemotherapy, testicular trauma, or symptoms of hypogonadism, and his semen analysis is normal.  
4. The patient reports regular menstrual cycles occurring every 28 to 30 days and lasting 3 to 5 days.  
5. She has no significant medical history and follows a healthy lifestyle, including regular exercise and a balanced diet.  
6. Gynecologic examination reveals no abnormalities, and secondary sexual characteristics are normal.  
7. Her BMI is 26.

1. An 82-year-old man with a history of atrial fibrillation presents to the emergency room complaining of sudden-onset, painless vision loss in his right eye starting 2 days ago.
2. When it started, he felt like a “curtain was pulled down” over his right eye but wasn't able to seek care immediately because it was snowing outside and he didn't want to travel in inclement weather.
3. A review of systems is significant for occasional palpitations and presyncope.
4. The patient’s medications include aspirin and carvedilol.
5. He reports that he is a smoker with a 50-pack-year history.
6. The patient’s temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 112/72 mmHg, pulse is 84/min, and respirations are 14/min with an oxygen saturation of 97% on room air.
7. Physical exam reveals 20/800 vision in the right eye.
8. A fundoscopic exam of the right eye is shown in Figure A.
9. Physical and fundoscopic examinations of the left eye are unremarkable.

1. A 29-year-old female patient presents to the office with low back pain lasting five days.
2. She recently began a new job requiring extensive walking, often several miles daily throughout a large facility.
3. The pain is localized to her back without leg radiation, and she reports no traumatic incidents.
4. Her medication history includes only oral contraceptives.

1. A 42-year-old man presents to the urgent care clinic with low back pain.
2. He was working on a home improvement project the day prior to presentation when the pain started.
3. He describes the pain as "achy and sore." It is not positional and does not radiate.
4. He denies fevers, chills, paresthesias, and bowel or bladder incontinence.
5. He has a history of a distal radius fracture 2 years ago from falling off a ladder.
6. He drinks 3 alcoholic beverages weekly and denies illicit drug use.
7. The patient’s temperature is 98.4°F (36.9°C), blood pressure is 124/80 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, and respirations are 16/min.
8. His body mass index (BMI) is 22.4 kg/m^2.
9. There is tenderness to palpation of his paravertebral lumbar region bilaterally.
10. Perineal and dermatomal sensation is symmetric and intact.
11. Strength is 5/5 to knee flexion/extension and ankle dorsiflexion/plantarflexion.
12. Patellar and Achilles reflexes are 2+ bilaterally.
13. Raising either leg while the patient is in the supine position does not elicit any pain.

1. A 35-year-old man comes to the physician because of pain and swelling of his right arm where he scraped it on a tree branch 2 days ago.
2. His temperature is 38.3°C (101°F).
3. Examination of the right forearm shows edema around a fluctuant erythematous lesion at the site of trauma.
4. The area is extremely tender to palpation.

1. A 60-year-old woman was referred to the emergency department with a history of abdominal discomfort and a palpable mass in the right iliac fossa.
2. She denied any change in her bowel habits or having experienced rectal bleeding.
3. She had a normal appetite and had no history of weight loss.
4. Before this admission, she was healthy, with no previous medical problems.
5. On examination, her vital signs were within normal limits.
6. She was mildly tender in the right iliac fossa and there was a large mobile mass, at least 10 cm in diameter, that was easily palpable in the right iliac fossa.
7. She was initially investigated with a computed tomography (CT) scan of the abdomen (Figure 1).
8. She underwent a colonoscopy that showed no intraluminal mucosal abnormalities or masses, but evidence of external compression at the cecum was noted.Coronal (A) and transverse (B) computed tomographic images show a large intra-abdominal cystic mass in the right iliac fossa.

1. A 55-year-old male comes to his primary care doctor for a routine wellness visit.
2. He reports feeling generally well without specific concerns.
3. His history reveals frequent alcohol consumption, high sodium dietary intake, a sedentary lifestyle, and class I obesity.
4. His vital signs show: temperature 97.5°F (36.4°C), blood pressure 167/108 mmHg, pulse 90/min, respiratory rate 15/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
5. Previous blood pressure readings from his last two visits were 159/100 mmHg and 162/99 mmHg.
6. The physician plans to address his blood pressure management.

1. A 43-year-old male patient attends a routine primary care visit where urinalysis reveals 3+ protein and 1–2 red blood cells per high-power field, with no other abnormalities.
2. He has no symptoms, no relevant family history, and denies smoking or alcohol use.
3. His vital signs include a temperature of 36.7°C (98.06°F), blood pressure of 130/82 mm Hg, and a pulse rate of 78/min.
4. Physical examination findings are unremarkable.

1. A 5-year-old girl was referred to ophthalmology care for evaluation of nystagmus.
2. Her medical history included esophageal atresia, small bowel obstruction, mild cognitive impairment, low tone, and increased reflexes.
3. Prenatal history was complicated by insulin-controlled gestational diabetes and polyhydramnios.
4. Her ocular history was notable for eye movement abnormalities since birth.
5. She had no family history of ocular disease.
6. On examination, her visual acuity was 20/150 OU and did not improve with correction (right eye, −1.50 [2.00] × 180; left eye, −1.00 [1.50] × 180).
7. Pupillary responses were normal.
8. Alternating vertical and torsional nystagmus was noted (Figure 1).
9. Specifically, 1 eye was noted to rise and intort while the other would fall and extort, followed by reversal of the vertical and torsional components in the opposite eye (Video).
10. The optic nerve and foveal reflexes were normal in both eyes.
11. Flash visual evoked potential (VEP) demonstrated strong ipsilateral activity of the occipital lobe.
12. Results of a previously obtained brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan were reported as normal.

1. A woman in her 40s presented with painful erythematous plaques on her trunk (Figure, A).
2. Skin lesions developed 2 months earlier and progressively spread.
3. She reported abdominal discomfort, weight loss, and vaginal bleeding.
4. A solid mass on her lower abdomen that had been palpable about 10 years prior had rapidly increased in size within the past few months.
5. Physical examination revealed erythematous plaques on the right chest and flank without warmth.
6. Punch biopsy of a lesion from the chest was sent for histopathological examination (Figure, B and C).
7. A, Erythematous plaques involving the right chest and flank at the initial presentation.
8. B and C, Large atypical cells with clear or eosinophilic cytoplasm forming papillary and glandular architectures are present in the deep dermis; lymphovascular invasion was observed in the superficial and deep dermis (hematoxylin-eosin).
9. D, Contrast-enhanced computed tomographic scan of the abdomen and pelvis showing a large heterogeneous mass in the right rectus abdominis muscle (blue arrowhead) and cystic lesion in the left ovary (pink arrowhead).

1. A 23-year-old woman presents to her psychiatrist concerned about her mood.  
2. She has felt tired and unwilling to engage in any activities lately.  
3. She states that her limbs feel heavy all the time and that completing any activity takes tremendous effort.  
4. She no longer finds any happiness in activities that she previously enjoyed.  
5. She struggles to sleep and at times can't sleep for several days.

1. A 34-year-old woman presented with 2 years of progressively worsening intermittent dysphagia, primarily to solids, especially meats, localized retrosternally.
2. She reported no heartburn, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, weight loss, or changes in bowel habits.
3. She reported no medications or comorbidities.
4. Physical examination was unremarkable.

1. Patient D is a 24-year-old  female with neurofibromatosis who presents with progressive pelvic and right leg pain

1. A 42-year-old man comes to the physician because of malaise, muscle and joint pain, and temperatures to 38.4°C (101.1°F) for 3 days.

1. A 35-year-old male injured his right shoulder while playing basketball.

1. A 30-year-old man presents to the emergency room with a laceration over the 4th metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint of his right hand.

1. Patient D is a 62-year-old  male who presents to your emergency room with complaints of chest pain

4. Patient D denies any radiation of his pain, or any exacerbation with deep inspiration

1. A 72-year-old woman presents with swelling in her left lower limb, which she first noticed two weeks ago.

1. A 46-year-old man presented with a left shoulder mass.

9. A whole-body positron emission tomographic and computed tomographic scan revealed an intensely hypermetabolic left shoulder mass and multiple hypermetabolic enlarged left axillary lymph nodes, with no distant metastases (Figure 1B).
10. Brain magnetic resonance imaging was negative for intracranial metastasis.A, Left shoulder giant fungating mass in a 46-year-old man.
11. B, Positron emission tomographic and computed tomographic (PET-CT) scan shows the hypermetabolic left shoulder mass and no distant metastases.

1. A 20-year-old male presents to the emergency department 6 hours after sustaining a punch to the head during a fistfight.

1. A 20-year-old male presents to the clinic six weeks after undergoing abdominal surgery for a gunshot wound, reporting diffuse, achy abdominal pain rated as 4/10.

1. A 25-year-old gravida 3 para 2 female is admitted to the hospital at 39 weeks' gestation in active labor.

1. A 6-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department 2 hours after injuring his arm when he fell out of a tree.

1. An otherwise healthy adult man presented with left upper eyelid swelling for 2 days.
2. This was accompanied by foreign-body sensation and discomfort of the left eye and was preceded by a week of general malaise without fevers or chills.
3. He denied vision changes, light sensitivity, or drainage from the eye.
4. He denied previous similar episodes of eyelid swelling or recurrent chalazia.

12. A, External photograph of the left eye demonstrating central upper eyelid margin ulceration with sparse lashes and surrounding edema.

1. A man in his 40s with a history of chronic blurry vision in both eyes (worse in the right eye) had latent extrapulmonary tuberculosis that had been treated with antitubercular therapy 1 year earlier.
2. Oral prednisone provided visual improvement.
3. However, the therapy was complicated by avascular hip necrosis that required total hip arthroplasty, and his visual symptoms recurred with corticosteroid tapering.
4. At presentation, his visual acuity was 20/150 OD and 20/15 OS.
5. The anterior segment was normal in both eyes.
6. Dilated ophthalmoscopic examination of the right eye revealed a diffuse subretinal yellow mass and an exudative retinal detachment temporal to the fovea (Figure 1).
7. Ophthalmoscopic examination of the left eye was normal.
8. B-scan of the right eye showed a dome-shaped choroidal lesion with an apical height of 3.4 mm and medium to high internal reflectivity.
9. Fluorescein angiography demonstrated heterogeneous leakage, and optical coherence tomography of the macula showed subretinal fluid with irregular retinal and choroidal thickening.
10. Results from extensive workup for infectious and autoimmune etiologies (including serum angiotensin-converting enzyme, lysozyme, lumbar puncture, magnetic resonance imaging of the brain and orbits, and computed tomography of the chest) were negative, except for positive purified protein derivative skin testing and positive interferon-γ release assay (QuantiFERON-TB Gold; Cellestis, Inc).
11. Large choroidal tuberculoma at presentation.
12. In a fundus view of the right eye, a moderate amount of subretinal fluid is seen adjacent to the lesion, involving the fovea center.
13. B-scan (not shown) measured an apical height of 3.4 mm.

1. A 45-year-old male experiencing shortness of breath is brought to the emergency department after shoveling snow.

3. He has a history of asthma treated with inhaled budesonide and formoterol, and is currently taking ciprofloxacin for a urinary tract infection.

1. A 69-year-old man presents to his primary care physician for a general checkup.

1. A 52-year-old male patient returns for a follow-up visit.
2. Six weeks ago, he was hospitalized for a pulmonary abscess in the peripheral region of the left lower lung lobe and underwent transthoracic tube drainage.

1. A healthy 2-year-old girl is brought to the office for a routine well-child visit.

3. On physical examination, she has mild bowlegs (10-degree genu varum).

1. Patient D is a 63-year-old  female with history of renal cell carcinoma who presents with acute neck and arm pain

7.

1. A 17-year-old boy presents to the emergency department after a car accident.

1. An 8-year-old boy presented to the pediatric emergency department with 2 weeks of fatigue and 3 days of double vision, ptosis, and painless periorbital swelling of the left eye.  
2. Medical history was unremarkable with no recent weight loss, travel, or trauma.

11. The remainder of the neurologic examination results were normal.An 8-year-old boy presented with 2 weeks of painless proptosis of the left eye (A) accompanied by upper eyelid ptosis and ophthalmoplegia of the left eye (B).

1. A 34-year-old woman comes to the office because of a 3- to 4-week history of swelling of her legs and a 9-kg (20-lb) weight gain.
